approach: Add `check_subjective_method(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs and append one `step!(check_subjective_method(reading, request));` line at the end of `refusing_check` (checks.rs, after `check_reading_references`, so no pinned neighbour moves). It scans only `plain_request_prose(request)` (terms.rs:189), which already drops generated root-cause lines, quoted spans, example lists, paths and fenced code; there is no summary scan and no root-cause skip. Trigger (revised after round 2, answers findings 2 and 3): a plain-prose line triggers when it holds a `VISIBLE_NOUNS` word (outcome.rs:49-63, reused, not edited; `site` right after `call` ignored) and either (A) a self-subjective phrase: newcomer, newcomers, easy to follow, easy to understand, easy to read, understandable; or (B) a clarity phrase (how clear, clear to, clear for, clarity) together with an audience word on the same line (newcomer, newcomers, beginner, beginners, novice, novices, first-time, reader, readers, visitor, visitors, audience, outsider). So 'Improve the clarity of the verifier report' and 'Make the error in the report clear to the operator' never trigger; 'a page clear to a newcomer', 'how clear the page is to a beginner' and 'explainer page easy to follow' do. Bare `readable` is not a phrase. Acceptance: ONE criterion of kind Behavior (as in `check_outcome_state`, outcome.rs:323-327) with four parts: (1) an independence word (independent, independently, fresh, separate, 'no part in', 'took no part', 'did not build') plus a reader word (reader, model, reviewer, judge); (2) a persona: persona, newcomer(s), novice, beginner, first-time, outsider, layperson, 'new' followed by user/reader/visitor/contributor/hire, or 'reads it as a/an' / 'reads as a/an' (not a bare 'as a'); (3) a 1-to-5 scale: 1 to 5, 1-5, 1–5, 1 through 5, out of 5, out of five, a digit 1-5 followed by 'of 5' or 'of five' (answers finding 1: the defaults.toml wording 'a rating below 4 of 5'), 5-point, five-point, or a `d/5` token; (4) a pass threshold: a threshold word (minimum, at least, below, under, threshold, 'no less than') followed within three words by a digit 1-5, or a digit followed within two words by 'or above/higher/more' or 'and above'. The error names the parts the closest Behavior criterion lacks (all four if none) and tells the reader to state the method as a Behavior criterion before the build. A corpus test takes the user's outcome-check default sentence word for word from defaults.toml (include_str!) and proves that a Behavior criterion holding it is accepted, so the gate cannot drift from the user's own default. Root cause in the doc comment: no required verification method for subjective quality at the reading gate (jobs 20261014-163844-c2kt and 20261015-064153-wekz); the doc also names the extension points for audience words and personas. Tests: unit tests in reading.rs, refusal-corpus cases with new input-form tags, a declared-share test, a reading-rules line in briefs.rs, a CHANGELOG entry and a C8 row in defaults-loop.md.

decisions.choice: Put the check at the reading gate as one new `step!` line at the end of `refusing_check`; no prompt, defaults.toml or job-specific code.
decisions.reason: The fault starts where a reading with a subjective outcome and no method is accepted. `check_reading_acceptance` (checks.rs:487) wraps `refusing_check` and is reached by the build path, `check_reading_text` (replay.rs:54) and `athena check-reading`, so one step covers all. The corpus test `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` forces a refusing case. Appending after `check_reading_references` keeps the adjacency tests passing.

decisions.reason: `plain_request_prose` already drops the 'Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:', 'Failure class:', 'Cause:' and 'Introspection ... prevention it proposed:' lines when the anchor is present (terms.rs:62-80, 189-207; hestia.rs:480-503). This job's own request, whose cause text quotes 'a page is clear to a newcomer', therefore has no trigger left, with no special case. decisions.choice: The method must be one criterion of kind Behavior holding all four parts, with the scale matcher also accepting '<digit> of 5' and 'of five' (answers finding 1).
decisions.reason: `check_outcome_state` accepts only Behavior (outcome.rs:304-307, 323-327): a content criterion checks a file, not a run. defaults.toml:89 (outcome-check) says 'a rating below 4 of 5 blocks completion'; a gate that refused that wording would refuse the user's own prescribed method. A corpus Accept case and a unit variant use that sentence word for word, read from defaults.toml by include_str!, so any later drift of the default or the matcher fails a test. Tight persona and threshold matchers still stop incidental wording ('as a reference', a stray digit) from satisfying the gate. Behavior criteria are also screened by `check_criteria_evidence`, so the method names a command the verifier can run (for example `athena audience`).

rejected.option: Accept any criterion kind with loose phrase matches
rejected.why: A content criterion or loose wording satisfies the gate with no check that runs, so the class can recur.

rejected.option: Accept parts spread over several criteria

rejected.option: Require the threshold to be at least 4

rejected.option: Copy the defaults.toml sentence into the matcher as the only accepted form
rejected.why: Refuses honest variants such as '1 to 5 ... at least 4'; the four-part matcher accepts both.

decisions.choice: Two trigger tiers (answers finding 2): self-subjective phrases (newcomer, easy to follow/understand/read, understandable) trigger with a visible noun; clarity phrases (how clear, clear to, clear for, clarity) trigger only when an audience word (newcomer, beginner, novice, first-time, reader, visitor, audience, outsider) is on the same line. `VISIBLE_NOUNS` is reused without editing; `site` right after `call` is ignored.
decisions.reason: 'report' and 'dashboard' are in VISIBLE_NOUNS (outcome.rs:59,62), so 'Improve the clarity of the verifier report' would trigger on the single-tier design though it asks for a technical output, not an audience judgement. Requiring an audience word for the clarity phrases keeps those requests out, while 'a page clear to a newcomer' and 'how clear a page is to a beginner' still trigger. One noun list means the two checks cannot drift; editing VISIBLE_NOUNS would also widen `delivery_verbs` (outcome.rs:200-205), a different rule. Accept cases pin 'Improve the clarity of the verifier report' and 'Make the error in the report clear to the operator'.

rejected.why: Refuses ordinary code requests; criterion 6 says it must not.

risks.risk: The trigger refuses ordinary code requests or misses real subjective wording.
risks.mitigation: A phrase needs a VISIBLE_NOUNS word on the same plain-prose line; clarity phrases additionally need an audience word, so 'clarity of the verifier report' and 'report clear to the operator' pass. Bare `readable` is not a phrase, `call site` is ignored, and quoted spans, paths, example lists and generated lines are dropped by `plain_request_prose`. Accept cases pin these. Step 6 runs the full athena-core suite before tests are added; if an existing case is refused, narrow the trigger, not the test. The 5% share is declared so replay does not hold the job.

risks.risk: 'Make the verifier report easy to read' (a technical report with a self-subjective phrase) is refused although it is a code request.
risks.mitigation: Intended and documented in the doc comment limits: 'easy to read' on an audience-facing noun is a subjective outcome, and the error says exactly how to satisfy the gate with one Behavior criterion. The higher refusal rate is declared.

risks.risk: The gate refuses the user's own outcome-check wording (finding 1).
risks.mitigation: The scale matcher accepts '<digit> of 5' and 'of five'; the corpus case subjective-defaults-sentence-method-accepted takes the sentence from defaults.toml by include_str!, so a mismatch fails a test instead of reaching a reader.

risks.risk: This job's own request, or a retry, is refused because its cause text quotes 'clear to a newcomer'.
risks.mitigation: `plain_request_prose` drops the 'Fix the root cause...', 'Failure class:', 'Cause:' and 'Introspection...' lines when the anchor sentence is present. The Accept corpus case subjective-cited-in-root-cause-request pins this, and generated_request_has_the_generators_shapes fails first if hestia rewords a line.

risks.risk: A request body holding the outcome on a non-generated line of a root-cause job is read as the request's own statement and refused.
risks.mitigation: Intended: such a line is the request's own sentence. The Refuse case subjective-root-cause-own-sentence-no-method pins it.

risks.risk: The Behavior method criterion trips an earlier check (criteria evidence, code survey, environment reach, outcome state) in the Accept cases, notably when it carries the verbatim defaults sentence.
risks.mitigation: The method criterion starts with a command (`athena audience`) and uses the sentence 'For audience-facing quality ... blocks completion.' only, leaving out the 'Prose-only' sentence. A corpus Accept case proves the pair passes the whole gate. If another check refuses the fixture wording, the producer rewords the fixture prefix, not the check or the defaults sentence.

risks.risk: The persona or threshold matchers reject honest wordings of a real method (for example a persona 'an operator').
risks.mitigation: The error lists the accepted forms and names the missing part; the doc comment names the persona word list in surveys.rs as the extension point. Widening a list is a one-line change.

risks.risk: The corpus case for 20261015-064153-wekz is rebuilt from the brief and may differ from the recorded request.
risks.mitigation: Records are absent from the snapshot. The case source says 'rebuilt from the job brief' and uses the introspection's stated shape; the cases pin the rule's behaviour, not the job's wording.

risks.risk: The briefs.rs byte-size assertion (under 2750, measured 2718) fails with the new rule line.
risks.mitigation: Raise the bound once to 3000 with the measured size in the comment; the line stays at most 220 characters.

risks.risk: Clippy or fmt fails on the new code at the final run (criterion 8).
risks.mitigation: Step 13 runs `cargo fmt --all` and then the three exact check commands; every helper is used by the check, so there is no dead-code warning.

Also read the candidate diff of checks.rs.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in reading.rs. Build `terms_reading(&[])` (reading.rs:6614, a docs reading that passes every check) with the request 'Write an explainer page on how firstmate handles work that is clear to a newcomer.' and criteria that give no method. Call the production `refusing_check` through `refuser_for` (reading.rs:6609), `check_subjective_method` and `check_reading_acceptance`. Assert the refuser is Some("check_subjective_method"), the error starts 'the reading was refused because' and contains 'independent', 'persona', 'rating', 'threshold', 'behavior' and 'before the build', and has no newline. A second assertion uses a generated root-cause request whose own sentence asks for the same outcome: refused too. A third assertion: 'how clear the explainer page is to a first-time reader' is refused (clarity tier with an audience word).
demonstrations.observes: The gate refuses under the check's own name and the error names the missing independent model reader, persona, 1 to 5 rating and pass threshold.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `step!` line `refuser_for` returns None and the Some assert fails. Without the function, or with a trigger that misses 'clear to a newcomer', `unwrap_err()` panics. If the error lacks the missing parts the string asserts fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `refusing_check`, `check_reading_acceptance` and `check_subjective_method`; fixtures `terms_reading` and `refuser_for` exist (reading.rs:6609-6618); function and step line are added by steps 2-5, the test by step 7. No double: the reading is a plain struct value built in the test.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in reading.rs (step 7). (a) `subjective_method_stated_is_accepted`: the criterion-3 reading plus a Behavior criterion 'Run `athena audience`: an independent model reader that had no part in building the page reads it as a newcomer and rates it from 1 to 5; a rating below 4 blocks completion.' is accepted by `check_reading_acceptance(&reading, request, None, &[], None)`; further accepted variants: the defaults.toml wording 'a fresh model reader that took no part in the work rates the live result as a newcomer, and a rating below 4 of 5 blocks completion' (finding 1), '4/5', 'out of 5', 'at least 4', '4 or above', and a persona 'a new user' (finding 3). (b) `subjective_method_partial_is_refused`: variants drop one part at a time (independent reader, persona, scale, threshold); each is refused and the error names exactly the dropped part; a variant with the threshold word and the scale digits but no digit next to the threshold word is refused; a variant with the full method only in a Content criterion is refused. (c) `subjective_method_ignores_other_requests`: 'Refactor the page renderer into two functions', 'Clear the cache when the page reloads', 'Make each call site readable', 'Make the page output machine-readable', 'Make the JSON output human-readable', 'Improve the clarity of the verifier report', 'Make the error in the report clear to the operator', a quoted mention (Rename the "newcomer" page template) and a root-cause request whose cause line quotes the newcomer outcome are all accepted.
demonstrations.observes: The full Behavior method (including the user's own default wording) is accepted, each partial or content-only method is refused naming the gap, ordinary and technical-clarity requests pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the check demanded more than the four parts or detected none, the accept assertions fail. If the scale matcher lacked '<digit> of 5', the defaults-wording variant is refused and fails. If it ignored the Behavior kind, the content-only refusal fails. If the trigger ignored the artifact noun, the audience-word rule for clarity phrases, the hyphen boundary or quotes, the ordinary requests are refused. If it refused everything, the plain refactor fails.
demonstrations.seam: Same production entry points as criterion 3; `Reading` built with existing `terms_reading`; request strings are inputs; no double. Tests added by step 7.

demonstrations.method: Step 10 adds `subjective_cases()` chained in `cases()` (refusal_corpus.rs:281), built with the existing `case(...)`, `with_behavior` and `base_reading`, run through `refusing_check` by `run` (refusal_corpus.rs:2039). Input forms handled and their cases (new tags appended to INPUT_FORMS, array length 41 grows by the number added, and `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms` at line 2097 requires each tag to have a case): subjective-outcome-no-method → Refuse cases subjective-explainer-page-no-method (source 20261014-163844-c2kt, rebuilt from the job brief), subjective-loop-page-no-method (shape of 20261015-064153-wekz: a loop improving the explainer page until it is easy to follow, rebuilt from the brief), subjective-root-cause-own-sentence-no-method (root-cause request helper with the sentence 'The explainer page must be clear to a newcomer.' in the request's own first paragraph), subjective-clear-to-first-time-reader-no-method; subjective-method-stated → Accept subjective-explainer-page-method-stated, subjective-loop-page-method-stated, and subjective-defaults-sentence-method-accepted (the Behavior criterion is 'Run `athena audience`: ' plus the outcome-check sentence from defaults.toml, extracted from `include_str!("../../../defaults.toml")` between 'For audience-facing quality' and 'blocks completion.', not retyped; finding 1), subjective-new-user-persona-method-stated (finding 3); subjective-word-without-artifact → Accept subjective-clear-the-cache, subjective-machine-readable-output, subjective-call-site-readable, subjective-plain-refactor; subjective-technical-clarity → Accept subjective-clarity-of-verifier-report and subjective-clear-to-operator-report (finding 2); subjective-quoted-or-generated → Accept subjective-quoted-newcomer and subjective-cited-in-root-cause-request (generated request whose cause and prevention text quote the newcomer outcome); subjective-method-partial-or-content-only → Refuse subjective-method-without-threshold, subjective-method-without-independent-reader, subjective-method-in-content-criterion-only. The existing `generated_root_cause_request` (refusal_corpus.rs:742) hard-codes its cause; step 10 moves its body into a helper taking the cause text, prevention text and sentence, and the old function calls it. Each Refuse case expects `Expected::Refuse("check_subjective_method")`.
demonstrations.observes: Every new Refuse case is refused by exactly check_subjective_method, the accepted counterparts pass, and the coverage tests pass. I cannot run the file; I cite only the ids this plan adds.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the step line the Refuse cases return accepted and `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` fails. `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` fails if no case is refused by this check. `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms` fails if a new tag has no case. The defaults-sentence Accept case fails if the scale matcher lacks '<digit> of 5'.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point `refusing_check` via corpus `run`; fixtures `case`, `with_behavior`, `base_reading`, `repo_files` and `generated_root_cause_request` exist; the cases, the tags, the defaults.toml include_str! and the helper split are added by step 10.

demonstrations.method: `subjective_method_refusal_is_declared_intended` mirrors `environment_reach_refusal_is_declared_intended` (refusal_corpus.rs:2265): `athena_core::reading::replay_declaration` on a Behavior criterion 'The change refuses more readings: expected 5% of newly refused readings' gives share Some(5); the collapsed CHANGELOG (`include_str!`, as at refusal_corpus.rs:2255) holds 'check_subjective_method', 'higher refusal rate is intended' and 'expected 5% of newly refused readings'; the doc comment calls the 5% an estimate. The narrow trigger is shown by the Accept corpus cases for ordinary and technical-clarity requests (criterion 5).
demonstrations.observes: The declared share parses as 5; the text is in the doc and the changelog; the ordinary-request cases are accepted by the corpus run.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the changelog or doc omits the declared share, or the parser reads another number, the test fails. If the trigger is too wide, the accepted ordinary-request cases fail.
demonstrations.seam: `replay_declaration` is public and exists (used at refusal_corpus.rs:2217); CHANGELOG read with `include_str!` as sibling tests do; test added by step 10.

open_questions: User: Should the check later require the stated pass threshold to be at least 4 of 5, as the outcome-check default says, or is any stated threshold enough? This plan accepts any stated threshold and only requires that one exists.
